reason: The repository title says Holder's inequality while its gloss says duality of L^p spaces. THM-M-0279 separately owns the product-integral Holder inequality. The accepted intake therefore preserves the Lp-duality family but explicitly leaves the exact source theorem, measure hypotheses, exponent range, endpoint policy, scalar field, pairing convention, and surjectivity variant open. These choices produce inequivalent propositions, so selecting one in the statement phase would invent or substitute mathematics.
unresolved_inputs: immutable source edition, exact theorem/page, transcription, and errata disposition
real or complex scalar field and bilinear or sesquilinear pairing convention
measure-space assumptions needed for the representation/surjectivity direction
exponent encoding, conjugacy convention, and whether p = 1 or p = infinity is included
exact direction, uniqueness, norm equality, and isometric-isomorphism formulation
zero-measure, null-space, infinite-measure, and endpoint boundary policy
independent approval of the source-to-canonical-statement mapping
lean_surface_assessment: The pinned Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.Holder module elaborates and exposes MeasureTheory.Lp, StrongDual, ContinuousLinearMap.lpPairing, and lpPairing_eq_integral. This supplies the bounded canonical pairing, not the representation/surjectivity theorem requested by the Lp-duality gloss. The checked StatementProbe is infrastructure evidence only and receives no canonical-statement or proof credit.
retry_condition: An accountable source review must preserve and hash an immutable edition, select and transcribe one exact Lp-duality theorem, settle every listed hypothesis and convention, audit errata, and independently approve the mapping. A later statement run can then encode that exact claim, minimize pinned imports, fingerprint its elaborated expression, check transports, and run removed-hypothesis, changed-domain, binder-scope, and boundary mutations.
